title: Regular equations for the diagonal of a standard-smooth affine chart
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a standard-smooth homomorphism of commutative rings of relative dimension $d>0$. Put $W=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R A)$ and let $\Delta:\operatorname{Spec}A\to W$ be the diagonal, defined by the multiplication map $A\otimes_R A\to A$. For every point $w$ in the image of $\Delta$, there is an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $w$ in $W$ such that the kernel ideal of $\Delta^{-1}(U)\to U$ is generated by a $B$-regular sequence of length $d$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

source.place: Tag 067R (section of a smooth morphism is regular); explicit standard-smooth affine diagonal computation in WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/RegularImmersion.lean:336-375

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-standard-smooth-etale-polynomial-chart] to the standard-smooth map $R\to A$. It gives an etale $R$-algebra map $\psi:R[X_0,\ldots,X_{d-1}]\to A$ whose restriction to constants is the given map. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat], this chart is flat.

For $0\le i<d$ set $r_i=1\otimes\psi(X_i)-\psi(X_i)\otimes1$ in $T=A\otimes_R A$, and let $\mu:T\to A$ be multiplication. The $d$ elements $r_i$ form a weakly regular sequence by [lem-sc-flat-polynomial-diagonal-differences-weakly-regular], using flatness from step 1. Each $r_i$ lies in $\ker\mu$ because both tensor terms multiply to $\psi(X_i)$. The map $\mu$ is surjective since $a=\mu(a\otimes1)$ for every $a\in A$.

Apply [lem-sc-etale-polynomial-diagonal-kernel-clearance] to the etale chart $\psi$. It supplies $e\in T$ with $\mu(e)=1$ and $e\ker\mu\subseteq(r_0,\ldots,r_{d-1})$. Thus $\mu$, the list $(r_i)$, and $e$ satisfy every hypothesis of [lem-sc-affine-regular-immersion-kernel-criterion]: surjectivity and kernel membership are from step 2, weak regularity is from step 2, and $d>0$ is in the item statement. The criterion gives an affine neighbourhood of each point of $W=\operatorname{Spec}T$ on which the ideal of $\operatorname{Spec}A\to W$ is generated by a weakly regular list of length $d$.

Fix $w$ in the diagonal image and take the affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and weakly regular generators from step 3. Its inverse image under the diagonal is nonempty because it contains a preimage of $w$, so its defining ideal $I$ is proper: if $I=B$, its zero locus is empty. The list generates $I$, hence $B/I\ne0$. Together with weak regularity, this is exactly a $B$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The diagonal of affine spectra is induced by $\mu$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so the ideal supplied by the criterion is the ideal of $\Delta^{-1}(U)\to U$ in the statement.

lean.statement: theorem exists_isRegular_diagonal_generators_of_isStandardSmooth {R : Type u} {A : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) [Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension d R A] : let W := Spec (CommRingCat.of (A ⊗[R] A)) let Δ := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' R : A ⊗[R] A →ₐ[R] A).toRingHom) ∀ w : W, w ∈ Set.range Δ → ∃ U : W.affineOpens, w ∈ U.1 ∧ ∃ r : List Γ(W, U.1), r.length = d ∧ RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular Γ(W, U.1) r ∧ Ideal.ofList r = RingHom.ker (Δ.app U.1).hom
